# Nitrogen — calculated thermodynamic functions

<!-- generated-by: sync-thermochemistry.mjs -->

Source: SRC-000515, NIST Chemistry WebBook / Chase (1998), retrieved 2026-10-06. These are calculations from dated fits, not new measurements. Values below are rounded to four decimal places for computational comparison; this is not a statement of physical precision. Uncertainty: UNKNOWN. Basis: **mol N2**.

sources.title: NIST Chemistry WebBook — molecular Nitrogen N2 GAS thermochemistry (6 October 2026 SI retrieval)
sources.organization: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.scope_note: Dated SI response for the existing NIST WebBook Nitrogen/N2 work owned by SRC-000102. Preserve that older node, aliases and spectroscopy supports; this retrieval is not a second independent work.
sources.scope: The retained species is molecular N2 (CAS 7727-37-9, InChI=1S/N2/c1-2), GAS, with one mole of N2 molecules containing two moles of nitrogen atoms. Bind MAT:0007:MOL:N2 at /ordinary_molecular_state; do not bind MAT:0007:ATOM:N or convert molecular functions to atomic functions by dividing by two. Source aliases including Nitrogen-14 and reported molecular weight do not specify isotopic fractions. Isotope composition and spin-isomer scope are UNSPECIFIED-IN-RETAINED-FIT. No dissociation, ionisation fraction, equilibrium composition or spin population is derived. Three GAS columns cover 100–500 K, 500–2000 K and 2000–6000 K. Keep both publisher rows at 500 K and 2000 K tied to their separate source columns; the rounded 2000 K heat capacities differ. Do not merge, average or impose continuity, infer a transition, or extrapolate below 100 K or above 6000 K. Existing atomic, liquid/cryogenic, phase-reference, cg-N and ammonia reaction owners remain separate. Retain the published enthalpy reference and any calculated reference residual rather than forcing zero. Retain Chase 1998, the reported March 1977 data review, January 2009 parameter fit, and 2026-10-06 retrieval as distinct provenance. The Shomate equations have no pressure variable; preserve their reported standard-state quantities and the separate gas, one-bar entropy datum without assigning an arbitrary sample pressure. Coefficient uncertainty and covariance are UNKNOWN. Separate CODATA entropy uncertainty, publisher output rounding and software arithmetic residuals are not coefficient uncertainty or independent measurement confirmation. This candidate capture and independent arithmetic review do not accept science, establish calorimetry or experimental replication, or complete Nitrogen thermophysics. A newly dated snapshot should record same_work_as SRC-000102; its old spectroscopy supports and identity ownership are preserved.
sources.reference: Chase, M.W., Jr. (1998), NIST-JANAF Thermochemical Tables, Fourth Edition. Retain March 1977 data review and January 2009 parameter-fit comments as distinct provenance.
